claims.sentence: Academic integrity consists of the behavioral rules in point 9 of the University's Internal Rules of Conduct and the ethical principles required to maintain trust in learning and research outcomes
A violation is any action or attempt to deceive while mastering a discipline, during current control, or during interim and final assessments
Plagiarism is using someone else's work in any form without citing sources and presenting it as your own
If you refuse to allow your work to be checked for originality when a violation is suspected, the violation is considered established
This regulation applies to all students enrolled in higher education programs at the University
A teacher may set an expected similarity threshold for assignments in the course program or assignment notification
The University uses plagiarism-checking software such as iThenticate, Turnitin, Antiplagiat, or other programs chosen by the teacher
The teacher must inform you of the suspected violation
If the originality check confirms the violation or you admit to it, the teacher must report the case to the Student Support and Development Department (SSDD) at the official email `319@innopolis.ru`
In cases of plagiarism, disciplinary measures apply to all students involved in the violation
You have 3 working days after receiving an email from the SSDD about a disciplinary measure to appeal the violation and the measure
To appeal, you must reply to the official SSDD email with your justification and evidence of your innocence
If you do not submit an appeal within this deadline, the teacher's decision becomes final and the disciplinary measures are applied
If you submit an appeal, the SSDD will schedule a Commission meeting via email and invite you within 10 working days of receiving your appeal
At the meeting, you may present evidence and arguments for your defense, and the Commission may ask follow-up questions
The Commission is a collegial body convened when you disagree with the violation fact

It consists of at least 3 members, including administrative staff, faculty, and potentially student council representatives, with a recommended composition of an SSDD employee, the Dean or deputy of the Faculty of Computer and Engineering Sciences, 1 faculty member, a program manager if available, and an official student self-government representative
The Commission makes decisions by simple majority vote
The consequences for violations are disciplinary measures applied to you
If you are caught violating the rules for the first time, you receive an unsatisfactory result (0-E) for the completed work, such as an assignment or interim assessment

If you are caught violating the rules a second time, you receive an unsatisfactory result (0-Р) for the discipline or module (or for multiple disciplines if two cases occur on different subjects), you are directed to retake the interim assessment, and you receive an official warning
The regulation does not specify the exact similarity thresholds that trigger a violation, only that a teacher may set one
The definition of plagiarism is cut off in the source text, so the full scope of what constitutes plagiarism is not provided
The regulation does not detail the exact procedures for how the Commission conducts its meetings or how evidence is formally submitted beyond the email invitation and verbal presentation
It does not specify what happens after a second violation or if there are consequences for a third violation
The regulation does not list the specific content of point 9 of the Internal Rules of Conduct that defines academic integrity
Course pages or other university documents may contain additional information, but this regulation is the primary local act governing disciplinary measures for academic integrity violations
